title: Inheritance
hook: A derived class gets the base’s accessible members except constructors and finalizers. You get one base class. Constructor chaining with base(...) is how identity is initialized before derived fields run.

sections.heading: Single base, what is inherited
sections.prose: class Derived : Base is the only class inheritance shape. Derived may also list interfaces. Public, protected, and internal members of the base are visible according to the modifiers in module 04. Constructors are not inherited: Derived must call a Base constructor, implicitly the parameterless one if it exists, or explicitly base(...). Finalizers are not inherited either; you still should not write them (module 14).

sections.heading: Constructor order
sections.prose: Field initializers in the derived type run, then the derived constructor body, but the base constructor runs first among constructor bodies. In practice: base ctor body, then derived ctor body, with field initializers sequenced as specified by the language (derived initializers before the derived body, base initializers before the base body). If you need to validate arguments before calling base, use a static helper in the argument list. Primary constructors on both base and derived can feed base(x) from derived parameters.

snippets.label: Single base and constructor chaining
snippets.explanation: LtiHandler has one base. The primary constructor forwards issuer to AuthHandler. There is no second class parent for, say, logging — inject a logger instead.

sections.heading: abstract and sealed on the type
sections.prose: abstract class: cannot new, may have abstract members. sealed class: cannot derive. sealed is the default you should want for workers and DTOs unless you designed a hierarchy. A sealed derived type on an abstract base is a common production pattern: closed set of providers, open for the base author only.

interviewTakeaways: One base class; constructors chain with base(...).
Constructors and finalizers are not inherited.
sealed is a design statement, not pessimism.
commonPitfalls: Forgetting that the base constructor runs before the derived body when reading instance virtual methods from a base ctor.
Public unsealed classes with no planned derived types.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS also requires super() before this in derived constructors. JS can mutate the prototype at runtime; C# hierarchies are fixed in metadata.
TS class extends one class and implements interfaces, similar on the surface. TS implements is erased; C# implements is runtime-checkable.
